newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to down, bears eye LSFO.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to down, bears eye LSFO.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to steady again Tuesday in quiet trade, with low sulphurs still pressured by oversupply despite forecasts for more below-normal East Coast weather later this week.
"There's so much oil around. The burns are up, but everyone's sitting on pretty good inventories," said one cash trader, noting low sulphurs seemed weaker than high sulphur grades.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped by about 25 cents to $18.50 a barrel, with February paper talked down more than a quarter to the $18.00 area, traders said.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour, still well-offered, slipped another 50 cents to below the $20 level despite reports of another NYPA tender for 100,000 barrels for Jan 21-31 delivery. Fixed-price bids only are due Wednesday at 1100 EST.
High sulphurs in New York again held steady, with 2.2 percent still quoted in the low-$17s.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent at $17.75-18.00 though some still thought the number was closer to $17.50. USG three percent was unchanged at $15.75-16.00, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate swing gas prices slipped a quarter Tuesday to the $4.30s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.94/mmBtu equivalent.
